bayesSampleMix

Contamination-aware Bayesian integration of probability and non-probability samples.

bayesSampleMix fits Gaussian, logistic and Poisson regressions to a trusted probability sample (P) combined with a non-probability sample (NP) in which an unknown subset of units may be incompatible with the target model. Each NP unit has a latent compatibility indicator; compatible units are pooled with the P sample, contaminated units are absorbed by a separate mixture component. You get

  • posterior inference for the target regression coefficients,
  • the posterior of the contamination fraction,
  • a filter score for every NP unit — its posterior probability of being compatible,
  • covariate-overlap diagnostics and reference fits (probability-only and naively pooled).

Why not just pool?

Strategy Bias under contamination Precision
Probability sample only none low
Naive pooling (treat all NP units as valid) yes — does not vanish as n grows high (but around the wrong value)
Contamination mixture adapts: uses only units the data deem compatible between the two

Installation

Once the package is on CRAN:

install.packages("bayesSampleMix")

The development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("dapr12/bayesSampleMix", build_vignettes = TRUE)

The package needs only base R (stats, graphics); knitr, rmarkdown, testthat and coda are suggested.

Quick start 

library(bayesSampleMix)

# simulated P and NP samples; 30% of NP units follow a different mechanism
d <- simulate_mixture_data("gaussian", n_prob = 150, n_nonprob = 300,
                           contamination = 0.3, beta = c(2, 5),
                           x_shift = 1.5, seed = 2026)

fit <- mixture_fit(
  formula      = y ~ x1,
  prob_data    = d$prob,
  nonprob_data = d$nonprob,
  family       = "gaussian",   # or "binomial", "poisson"
  model        = "Mjoint",     # or "M0", "M1"
  n_iter       = 3000,
  burnin       = 1000,
  thin         = 1,
  seed         = 123
)

summary(fit)                 # coefficients, contamination, filter scores, ESS
coef(fit)                    # posterior means
contamination(fit)           # posterior of 1 - pi
s <- filter_scores(fit)      # posterior P(compatible) for each NP unit
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x1 = c(-1, 0, 1)))
plot(fit, type = "trace")

# reference estimators
baseline_fit(y ~ x1, d$prob)                                   # probability only
baseline_fit(y ~ x1, rbind(d$prob, d$nonprob[names(d$prob)]))  # naive pooling

Interpreting the results

  • Coefficients are posterior means, standard deviations and equal-tailed credible intervals computed from the MCMC draws, with effective sample sizes and Monte Carlo standard errors. They describe the population represented by the P sample.
  • Contamination 1 - pi is the posterior probability that an NP unit is incompatible; contamination_realized is the share of the observed NP units allocated to the contaminating component.
  • Filter scores close to 0 flag units that the data consider incompatible with the target model; scores near 0.5 (high indicator entropy) indicate units that cannot be classified confidently.
  • Check overlap_diagnostics() before fitting and the trace plots after.

Models and algorithms

family target model contaminating density (M0/Mjoint) target update
gaussian N(x’β, σ²) N(μ0, τ²) conjugate Gibbs
binomial Bernoulli(logit⁻¹(x’β)) Bernoulli(q) Pólya–Gamma augmentation
poisson Poisson(exp(x’β)) Poisson(λ0) Laplace-proposal Metropolis–Hastings

Mjoint adds a covariate term that compares each NP unit’s continuous covariates with the P-sample distribution (Mahalanobis-type); M1 replaces the contaminating density by a rival regression. See ?mixture_fit and the vignettes:

vignette("introduction", package = "bayesSampleMix")
vignette("gaussian-model", package = "bayesSampleMix")
vignette("logistic-model", package = "bayesSampleMix")
vignette("poisson-model", package = "bayesSampleMix")

Relation to the original research code

The samplers, priors, initial values and defaults of the original scripts (mixture_filter.R, mixture_filter_glm.R, mixture_filter_pois.R) are preserved; the test suite checks that seeded fits reproduce them draw for draw. Differences and known approximations are documented in NEWS.md (notably the corrected M1 update, available in its original form via mixture_control(m1_update = "original")). The original Monte Carlo studies are in inst/validation/ and the rent-index application in inst/scripts/.
